question: A business starts with 12 units. It gains 52 (64). It multiplies by 5 (320). It multiplies by 8 (2560). It adds 5 (2565). It multiplies by 5 (12825). Another company has 100 units. How many units does the business produce?

A farm starts with 173 apples. It loses 8 (165). It adds 74 (239). It multiplies by 5 (1195). It adds 78 (1273). It multiplies by 5 (6365). At least half of 100 would be 50. How many apples does the farm have?

A project starts with 73 tasks. In the morning, 77 more are added (150). By midday, 17 additional arrive (167). By afternoon, 70 more surface (237). By end of day, 235 are completed. How many tasks remain active?
A farm starts with 151 chickens. It multiplies by 5 (755). It loses 323 (432). It divides by 2 (216). It loses 169. Two farms are mentioned. How many chickens remain?

A factory starts with 22 machines. In the morning, it multiplies by 9 (198). By afternoon, it multiplies by 8 (1584). It adds 18 (1602). It loses 729 (873). It multiplies by 4 (3492). It adds 18. How many machines does the calculation show?
A stock starts with 96 shares. It loses 72 (24). It gains 65 (89). It loses 28 (61). It loses 57. They convert shares from minutes to hours calculation. What is the final share count?

A project starts with 37 tasks. It gains 78 (115). It loses 77 (38). It multiplies by 4 (152). It loses 20 (132). It adds 63 (195). It multiplies by 3 (585). Tasks track through the day. How many total task-units are calculated?

A studio starts with 228 pieces. It adds 29 (257). It multiplies by 8 (2056). It multiplies by 9 (18504). It multiplies by 7 (129528). A rival studio has 1000 pieces. How many pieces does this studio create?

A garden starts with 53 plants. In the morning, 42 are lost (11). By afternoon, 67 are added (78). By evening, 43 arrive (121). They multiply by 9 (1089). By night, 73 are transplanted. How many plants are in the count?

Evan and Rose manage funds. They start with 82 dollars. They multiply by 4 (328). They add 5 (333). They lose 73 (260). They add 48 (308). They lose 164. Rose has 200 dollars. How much do they have combined?
A shop starts with 181 items. It adds 41 (222). It multiplies by 9 (1998). It multiplies by 4 (7992). A competitor removes 3660 from market. How many items does the shop have?

Lee and Pat count inventory. They start with 146 units. They multiply by 4 (584). They lose 101 (483). They lose 139 (344). They divide by 2 (172). They double (344). Pat has 300. One distractor: the old price was 89. How many units do they count?

A project starts with 139 hours. In the morning, 66 are logged (73). By afternoon, 55 more complete (18). By evening, 42 are added (60). It gains 44 (104). It gains 15 (119). It gains 47. Time tracking from minutes to hours noted. How many hours are recorded?

A company starts with 161 items. It multiplies by 3 (483). It multiplies by 2 (966). It adds 71 (1037). It loses 304 (733). It loses 23 (710). It loses 479. Morning to afternoon to evening progression. Time measured in minutes to hours. How many items remain?
A garden starts with 67 plants. It multiplies by 9 (603). It multiplies by 4 (2412). It adds 33 (2445). It adds 5 (2450). It adds 68 (2518). It adds 4. How many plants end up?

A bakery starts with 174 loaves. It adds 56 (230). It multiplies by 8 (1840). It multiplies by 6 (11040). It multiplies by 2 (22080). One distractor: previous stock was 95. How many loaves does it produce?

A store starts with 196 items. It adds 11 (207). It multiplies by 8 (1656). It multiplies by 3 (4968). It multiplies by 8 (39744). Morning rush, afternoon peak, evening closing all mentioned. One old price was 76. How much stock is calculated?

A warehouse starts with 210 units. It adds 36 (246). It adds 79 (325). It loses 201 (124). It multiplies by 7 (868). It multiplies by 8 (6944). It loses 1997 (4947). One distractor: competitor had 300. How many units remain?

A business starts with 145 units. It multiplies by 7 (1015). It multiplies by 5 (5075). It divides by 5 (1015). It multiplies by 4 (4060). Time measurement from minutes to hours noted. How much is the total?

Ben and Carol run inventory. They start with 176 items. They lose 163 (13). They add 11 (24). They add 25 (49). They lose 33 (16). They multiply by 8 (128). They lose 70 (58). One distractor: old shipment was 72. How many items do they track?

A factory starts with 213 components. It multiplies by 3 (639). It adds 78 (717). It loses 202 (515). It multiplies by 6 (3090). It loses 1997 (1093). Morning shift, afternoon shift, evening shift all recorded. How many components remain?

A warehouse starts with 115 boxes. It loses 44 (71). It adds 73 (144). It adds 36 (180). It loses 99 (81). It loses 34 (47). Time tracking minutes to hours mentioned. One distractor: next shipment is 200 boxes. How many boxes does it hold?
A counter starts with 25 items. It loses 18 (7). It adds 11 (18). It multiplies by 2 (36). It multiplies by 3 (108). All stages show the quantity's final state. How many does it end with?

A supply starts with 131 units. It gains 37 (168). It divides by 3 (56). It multiplies by 2 (112). It adds 80 (192). It divides by 4 (48). Morning to afternoon to evening timeline. How many units remain?

A project starts with 80 tasks. It gains 31 (111). It gains 25 (136). It divides by 2 (68). It gains 33 (101). It multiplies by 3 (303). It loses 92 (211). One distractor: previous plan had 47 tasks. How many are active?
